records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash / privacy; Data-access concerns; Council vote to shut cameras immediately and cancel the contract
records.Summary: Gardner City Council on August 17, 2026 agreed to turn off the city’s Flock cameras immediately and not renew the contract. KMBC reported August 18 that some cameras were covered by Tuesday, and that Gardner Police confirmed it discontinued all city Flock cameras and notified the vendor the contract was canceled. Council member Kelly Johnson said the vote covers only city-controlled cameras, not Johnson County or state units nearby. Resident Bradley Steinmetz of No Flock in Gardner said more than 1,200 vendors had access through the Flock system.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Camera count not published. County and state ALPRs in and around Gardner remain. Physical pickup timetable not published.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash; Mass-surveillance / Fourth Amendment / data-security concerns; Packed council meeting; Mayor terminate decision
records.Summary: After residents packed the August 17, 2026 council meeting, Fort Mitchell Mayor Greg Pohlgeers said the city would shut off and dismantle its five Flock readers immediately and would not renew. LINK nky reported the 2024 contract was 24 months for about $34,000. City Administrator Edwin King said staff would coordinate with Flock to end operations. FOX19 reported the mayor’s overnight announcement on August 19.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Immediate shutdown announced; vendor pickup timetable not published.

records.Primary_Reasons: Budget cuts; Public trust / privacy concerns; Police announcement to council; Related ODOT ALPR agreement killed
records.Summary: Winston Police Chief Brandon Sarti told City Council on August 17, 2026 that the department had canceled its Flock contract that day. NR Today reported eight cameras in Douglas County at about $24,000 a year, amid $215,000 in department budget cuts. Sarti said the lieutenant’s retirement plus the cancel should save about $217,000, and that if residents paying the bill do not want the cameras, the city is turning them off. Council also killed proposed Resolution 26-1237, an ODOT intergovernmental agreement that would have allowed ALPRs on Oregon Route 42. Mayor Christie Knutson said community outcry was part of the removal.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Physical removal timetable not published in the NR Today report.

records.Primary_Reasons: Officer alleged personal Flock / CJIS lookups; Police chief ended the Flock relationship as a direct result; Last camera removed
records.Summary: Stow Police Chief Michael Sallese announced August 18, 2026 that the department ended its Flock relationship as a direct result of alleged personal Flock and CJIS lookups by Officer Jason Rogers. The Boston Globe and boston.com reported the last remaining Flock camera was removed in early August; two other ALPRs came down earlier in 2026 after an effectiveness review. See FLK-2026-048. The department said it will evaluate safeguards before any future ALPR use and will bring a tighter request/approval policy to the Select Board.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Last camera removed early August 2026; two others removed earlier in 2026. Department may request ALPR data from outside agencies under a forthcoming policy.

records.Primary_Reasons: Privacy / constitutional concerns; National misuse reports; Sheriff suspend and dismantle while contract runs through 2028
records.Summary: Henry County Sheriff Wayne Davis suspended sheriff’s-office access to 14 Flock cameras (10 fixed, 4 mobile) on August 14, 2026 and said the office would explore early termination of a contract that runs through August 2028. WSLS reported August 17 that the office would begin dismantling the cameras in the coming days. Davis had said in July he would not renew in 2028; the August suspend moved that timeline up. This is a suspend / hardware pull, not a reported contract termination.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Contract still runs through August 2028. WSLS quoted Davis saying cameras may still record while sheriff’s-office access is off. Physical removal was announced as beginning in the days after August 17.

records.Primary_Reasons: Privacy / data-retention concerns; National ALPR backlash; Chief non-renewal pending 2027 legislative standards
records.Summary: Waukee Police Chief Chad McCluskey announced August 14, 2026 that the department will not renew its Flock Safety ALPR contract and will stop using the cameras pending the 2027 Iowa legislative session. The Des Moines Register reported 11 cameras and that none had been vandalized locally. Waukee was the first Des Moines metro city reported to drop Flock; Coralville canceled earlier in 2026.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Non-renewal / stop-use pending state legislation. Hardware removal timetable not published. Neighboring metro cities still contract with Flock per Register reporting.

records.Primary_Reasons: Privacy / data-sharing concerns; Public trust review; Chief deactivate pending legislative standards
records.Summary: Indianola Police Chief Rob Hawkins announced that beginning August 17, 2026 the department deactivated its eight Flock cameras and disabled outside-agency access to the data. KCRG and the Des Moines Register reported the program costs about $24,000 a year. Cameras remain installed pending coordination with Flock. Untied data will purge in 30 days. The department said it is listening to privacy concerns and watching the 2027 legislative session.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Suspend / deactivate, not a reported contract termination. Hardware remains up pending vendor coordination. May resume after review or 2027 legislation.

records.Primary_Reasons: Constitutional / privacy / public-trust concerns; Sheriff non-renewal after grant pilot; Fiscal responsibility
records.Summary: Henry County, Missouri, Sheriff Aaron N. Brown announced August 10, 2026 that the sheriff’s office will not renew its Flock Safety LPR agreement when the current term expires March 11, 2027. The program began earlier in 2026 through a State of Missouri grant. Brown said the system assisted investigations in its first five months but that public trust and constitutional principles weighed against continuing past the grant term.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Operational through March 11, 2027. Camera count not published in the Aug. 10 statement. Distinct from Henry County, Virginia (CAN-2026-105).
